Rashi on Berakhot 24a:10:1.english: Aren’t there buttocks - For they touch each other.

Rashi on Berakhot 24a:10:2.hebrew: וקוצה חלתה ערומה - ואף על פי שערום אסור לברך, אשה יושבת מותרת, שבישיבתה פניה שלמטה מכוסים בקרקע:
Rashi on Berakhot 24a:10:2.english: And separates her challah [while] naked - And even though one who is naked is forbidden to recite a blessing, a seated woman is permitted, because when she sits, her lower face [i.e., her private parts] is covered by the ground.

Rashi on Berakhot 24a:10:3.hebrew: אבל לא האיש - מפני שהביצים והגיד בולטין ונראין. ואף על פי שמגולות עגבותיו, והיינו סייעתא:
Rashi on Berakhot 24a:10:3.english: But not a man - Because the testicles and the penis protrude and are visible. And even though [the woman's] buttocks are exposed, [she is permitted]; and that is the support [for Rav Huna].

Rashi on Berakhot 24a:11:1.hebrew: כגון שהיו פניה טוחות - דבוקות ומכוסות בקרקע. טוחות — משמע לשון שעיעות, טיח חלק, שאינה בולטת — אפלטיירש"א בלע"ז:
Rashi on Berakhot 24a:11:1.english: For example, where her face was plastered - [That is,] pressed against and covered by the ground. Tuḥot implies an expression of smoothing, [like] a smooth plastering, so that it does not protrude — aplastredes [plastered] in Old French.

Rashi on Berakhot 24a:12:1.hebrew: בת שלש ובן תשע - שהוא זמן שהן באין לכלל ביאה:
Rashi on Berakhot 24a:12:1.english: A girl of three and a boy of nine - For that is the time when they enter the category of intercourse.

Rashi on Berakhot 24a:12:2.hebrew: בת י"א ובן י"ב - זמן שהן באות לכלל שערות ושדיהן נכונים, שמשם ואילך באות לכלל [ביאה] שאדם מתאוה להן:
Rashi on Berakhot 24a:12:2.english: [A girl] of eleven and [a boy] of twelve - [This is] the time that they reach the stage of [pubic] hair and their breasts are formed, for from then on they reach the stage of [intercourse] where a person lusts for them.

Rashi on Berakhot 24a:13:1.hebrew: התם אמר רבא - גבי תפילין תחת מראשותיו, דקאמר שמואל אפי' אשתו עמו — הלכה כשמואל:
Rashi on Berakhot 24a:13:1.english: There, Rava said - With regard to phylacteries under one's head, where Shmuel said [that it is permitted] even if his wife is with him, [that] the halakha is in accordance with Shmuel.

Rashi on Berakhot 24a:13:2.hebrew: הכא - גבי שנים שהם ישנים, דקא שרי שמואל באשתו עמו — מאי:
Rashi on Berakhot 24a:13:2.english: Here - Regarding [the case of] two who are sleeping, where Shmuel permits [reciting the Shema when] his wife is with him — what [is the ruling]?

Rashi on Berakhot 24a:13:3.english: [In a] weaving, did you weave them - Did you weave them in a single weaving?

Rashi on Berakhot 24a:14:1.hebrew: יצא שערו בבגדו - שנקב בגדו כנגד זקן התחתון, ויצא מן השער בנקב — מהו? מי הוי ערוה לקרות ק"ש כנגדו, או לא:
Rashi on Berakhot 24a:14:1.english: [If] his hair protruded through his garment - Where his garment had a hole opposite the lower beard [i.e., the pubic hair], and some of the hair protruded through the hole — what is [the ruling]? Does it constitute nakedness [such that it is forbidden] to recite the Shema facing it, or not?

Rashi on Berakhot 24a:14:2.english: Hair, hair - That is to say: What of it?

Rashi on Berakhot 24a:15:1.hebrew: לאסתכולי בה - אם אשת איש היא:
Rashi on Berakhot 24a:15:1.english: To look at her - [This applies] if she is a married woman.

Rashi on Berakhot 24a:15:2.hebrew: תכשיטין שבפנים - כומז, דפוס של בית הרחם שהיו עושין לבנותיהן, ונוקבין כותלי בית הרחם כדרך שנוקבין את האזנים, ותוחבין אותו כדי שלא יזדקקו להן זכרים:
Rashi on Berakhot 24a:15:2.english: Jewelry [worn] internally - [This is the] kumaz, a mold [in the shape] of the womb, which they would make for their daughters; and they would pierce the walls of the womb [i.e., the labia] just as they pierce the ears, and insert it, so that males would not have relations with them.

Rashi on Berakhot 24a:15:3.hebrew: עם תכשיטין שבחוץ - אצעדה וצמיד. הן הביאו אותן על כפרת הרהור עבירה, שנסתכלו בבנות מדין:
Rashi on Berakhot 24a:15:3.english: [Together] with external ornaments - [Namely,] an armlet and a bracelet. They brought them to atone for sinful thoughts, for having gazed at the daughters of Midian.

Rashi on Berakhot 24a:16:1.hebrew: לאשתו ולק"ש - אם טפח מגולה בה, לא יקרא ק"ש כנגדה:
Rashi on Berakhot 24a:16:1.english: Regarding his wife and for the recitation of Shema - If a handbreadth is exposed on her, he may not recite the Shema facing her.

Rashi on Berakhot 24a:17:1.english: A leg - [This applies] to a married woman.

Rashi on Berakhot 24a:17:2.hebrew: ערוה - להסתכל, וכן באשתו לק"ש:
Rashi on Berakhot 24a:17:2.english: Nakedness - [With regard to] looking [at it]; and likewise regarding his wife, for the recitation of the Shema.

Rashi on Berakhot 24a:17:3.hebrew: גלי שוק - וכתיב בתריה, תגל ערותך:
Rashi on Berakhot 24a:17:3.english: Uncover the leg - And it is written after it [in the following verse]: “Your nakedness shall be uncovered.”

Rashi on Berakhot 24a:17:4.hebrew: קולך ערב - מדמשבח לה קרא בגוה, שמע מינה תאוה היא:
Rashi on Berakhot 24a:17:4.english: Your voice is sweet - Since Scripture praises her for it, learn from this that it is [a source of] desire.

Rashi on Berakhot 24a:18:1.english: One who hangs his phylacteries - [If he hangs them] on a peg, his life will hang [in the balance].

Rashi on Berakhot 24a:19:1.hebrew: דורשי רשומות - קשרים וסתומים הכלולים בתורה. דורשי חמורות גרסינן, והיא היא:
Rashi on Berakhot 24a:19:1.english: Interpreters of intimations - [They interpret the] knots and obscure matters contained in the Torah. Our text reads: “Interpreters of weighty matters,” and it is one and the same.

Rashi on Berakhot 24a:19:2.hebrew: זה התולה תפיליו - שהתורה חייו של אדם, ורמז לך הכתוב שיתלו חייו:
Rashi on Berakhot 24a:19:2.english: This is one who hangs his phylacteries - For the Torah is a person's life, and Scripture hinted to you that his life will hang [in the balance].

Rashi on Berakhot 24a:1:1.hebrew: כל לנטורינהו טפי עדיף - להו מבזיוני. כמה שהוא מוזהר על שמירתן מן העכברים ומן הגנבים, טפי עדיף להו מבזיוני:
Rashi on Berakhot 24a:1:1.english: Whatever protects them more is preferable - [It is preferable] for them over degradation. Inasmuch as he is cautioned regarding safeguarding them from mice and from thieves, it is more preferable for them than degradation.

Rashi on Berakhot 24a:20:1.hebrew: ברצועה - והקציצה למטה, גנאי הוא להם. אבל תולה הוא אותם בקציצה, ותהא הקציצה מונחת על היתד, והרצועה למטה:
Rashi on Berakhot 24a:20:1.english: By the strap - And the box is below, [which] is a disgrace to them. But he may hang them by the box, so that the box is resting upon the peg, and the strap is below.

Rashi on Berakhot 24a:21:1.hebrew: בכיסתא תלה - בתוך תיקן היו, ותלה התיק:
Rashi on Berakhot 24a:21:1.english: He hung [them] in a pouch - They were inside their pouch, and he hung the pouch.

Rashi on Berakhot 24a:23:1.hebrew: שגיהק - ריט"ייר בלע"ז — פעמים שאדם מוציא מגופו לפיו נפיחה מתוך שובעו, וריחה כריח המאכל שאכל:
Rashi on Berakhot 24a:23:1.english: That he belched - Roter in Old French — at times a person emits from his body into his mouth a blast of air out of fullness, and its smell is like the smell of the food that he ate.

Rashi on Berakhot 24a:23:2.hebrew: פיהק - באליי"ר בלע"ז — חיך מלקוחיו פותח להוציא רוח הפה מלא, כאדם שרוצה לישן או שעמד משינה:
Rashi on Berakhot 24a:23:2.english: [He] yawned - *Baaillier* in Old French — he opens the palate of his jaws to emit the breath of the mouth fully, like a person who wants to sleep or who arose from sleep.

Rashi on Berakhot 24a:23:3.hebrew: ונתעטש - שטרנוד"ר בלע"ז. ויש שדורשים: גיהק — נוטריקון גו הקים (שטריליי"ר); פיהק — פיו הקים:
Rashi on Berakhot 24a:23:3.english: And sneezed - Esternuder in Old French [meaning to sneeze]. And there are those who interpret: Gihak is a notarikon [an acronym for] gev hekim [he raised his body] — estrillier [in Old French, to stretch]; pihek [is an acronym for] piv hekim [he raised his mouth, opening it wide].

Rashi on Berakhot 24a:2:1.english: In a kova - That is their pouch [for the phylacteries].

Rashi on Berakhot 24a:2:2.hebrew: למורשא דכובע - שהתפילין נכרין בבליטתן בקצה הכיס, והוא כמורשא:
Rashi on Berakhot 24a:2:2.english: The protrusion of the pouch - For the phylacteries are discernible by their bulge at the edge of the pouch, and it is like a protrusion.

Rashi on Berakhot 24a:3:1.hebrew: צייר להו בכילתא - ביריעה הפרוסה סביבו' מטתו, קושרן:
Rashi on Berakhot 24a:3:1.english: He would tie them in the bed curtain - In the curtain spread around his bed, he would tie them.

Rashi on Berakhot 24a:3:2.hebrew: ומפיק למורשהון לבר - בליטת הקשר, שהתפילין בולטין מן היריעה, היה הופך לצד החוץ, ולא לצד המטה:
Rashi on Berakhot 24a:3:2.english: And project their bulge outward - The bulge of the knot, where the phylacteries protrude from the curtain — he would turn [it] toward the outside, and not toward the side of the bed.

Rashi on Berakhot 24a:3:3.english: On a bench - [That is,] a bench.

Rashi on Berakhot 24a:4:1.hebrew: יום טבילה הוה - יום שטבלה אשתו, דהוה ליה ליל תשמיש. והיינו כשמואל, דאמר: אפילו אשתו עמו:
Rashi on Berakhot 24a:4:1.english: It was the day of immersion - The day that his wife immersed, so that it was a night of marital relations for him. And this is in accordance with Shmuel, who said: Even [if] his wife is with him.

Rashi on Berakhot 24a:4:2.hebrew: ולאגמורן הלכה למעשה - מה שצוני להביאם לו, לא עשה אלא ללמדני הלכה לעשות מעשה כשמואל:
Rashi on Berakhot 24a:4:2.english: And to teach us the practical halakha - That which he commanded me to bring them to him, he did only to teach me the halakha, to act in practice in accordance with [the view of] Shmuel.

Rashi on Berakhot 24a:5:1.hebrew: ואפילו אשתו עמו - שיחזיר פניו, דכל זמן שהן פונים פנים כנגד פנים, פשיטא ליה דאסור, דאיכא הרהור נגיעת ערוה על ידי אברי תשמיש:
Rashi on Berakhot 24a:5:1.english: And even [if] his wife is with him - [That is,] that he turns his face away [and recites]; for as long as they are facing face-to-face, it was obvious to him that it is forbidden, because there is lustful thought [from] contact with nakedness via the organs of intercourse.

Rashi on Berakhot 24a:6:1.hebrew: אשתו כגופו - ורגיל בה, וליכא הרהור כולי האי:
Rashi on Berakhot 24a:6:1.english: His wife is like his [own] body - And he is accustomed to her, so there is not so much [lustful] thought.

Rashi on Berakhot 24a:8:1.hebrew: בשלמא לרב יוסף - דאמר אשתו היא דשריא, אבל אחר לא — מתרץ להו למתניתא: הא באשתו, הא באחר. והא דקתני בני ביתו — אינו אשתו:
Rashi on Berakhot 24a:8:1.english: Granted, according to Rav Yosef - Since he said that it is [only] his wife who is permitted, but another [person] is not, he resolves the baraitot: this [one is] regarding his wife, [and] this [one is] regarding another [person]. And that which [the baraita] taught, “members of his household” — is not [referring to] his wife.

Rashi on Berakhot 24a:9:1.english: [If] he was sleeping in bed and the members of his household - And his wife is included in [the category of] “his household.”

Rashi on Berakhot 24a:9:2.hebrew: לדידי נמי - בין אשתו, בין אחר — פלוגתא דהני תנאי היא:
Rashi on Berakhot 24a:9:2.english: According to my [view] as well - Whether [regarding] his wife or [regarding] another [person], it is the dispute of these Tannaim.

Tosafot on Berakhot 24a:2:1.hebrew: והא תני רבי חייא מניחן בכובע תחת מראשותיו - ואם תאמר: אימא בכובע שלא כנגד ראשו — שהרי בברייתא דלעיל נמי תני "תחת מראשותיו", ולא פריך מיניה, משום דמצינן לפרושי שלא כנגד ראשו. ואומר הרב: דא"כ, מאי איריא בכובע? אפילו שלא בכובע נמי! אלא ש"מ דמיירי אפילו כנגד ראשו. ומ"מ קשיא: לישני דמיירי באשתו עמו, דבעיא כלי בתוך כלי! וצ"ע:
Tosafot on Berakhot 24a:2:1.english: "Didn’t Rabbi Ḥiyya teach: He places them in a pouch under his head?" - And if you say: Say [that it means] in a pouch, [placed] not aligned with his head — for in the baraita above as well it teaches "under his head," and [the Gemara] does not raise an objection from it, because we are able to explain [it as meaning] not aligned with his head! And the Rabbi says: For if so, why specifically in a pouch? Even not in a pouch as well! Rather, conclude from this that [Rabbi Ḥiyya] is dealing with even [placing them directly] aligned with his head. And nevertheless it is difficult: Let [the Gemara] answer that it is dealing with [a case where] his wife is with him, which requires a vessel within a vessel! And it requires further study.

Tosafot on Berakhot 24a:5:1.hebrew: שנים שהיו ישנים במטה - וא"ת: והלא רואה ערות עצמו? וי"ל: שיוציא ראשו לחוץ. וא"ת: והרי לבו רואה את הערוה? וי"ל: דקסבר לבו רואה את הערוה מותר; אי נמי, חוצץ בבגדו כנגד לבו:
Tosafot on Berakhot 24a:5:1.english: "Two who were sleeping in a bed" - And if you say: But does he not see his own nakedness? And one can say: That he extends his head outside [the blanket]. And if you say: But behold, his heart sees the nakedness? And one can say: That he holds [that when] his heart sees the nakedness, it is permitted; or alternatively, he creates a barrier with his garment opposite his heart.

Tosafot on Berakhot 24a:9:1.hebrew: והתניא היה ישן במטה ובני ביתו וכו' - פי' רש"י: אשתו בכלל ביתו. ולא נהירא: חדא — דלא אשכחן אשתו דמקריא בני ביתו; ועוד — לפירושו, הול"ל "והא קתני כאן", כיון דאברייתא דלעיל קאי, אבל מדקאמר "והתניא", משמע דברייתא אחרת היא. ואומר ה"ר יוסף, דגרסינן: היה ישן במטה, ואשתו ישנה בצדו — לא יחזיר פניו ויקרא, אא"כ היתה טלית מפסקת בינו לבינה:
Tosafot on Berakhot 24a:9:1.english: "And wasn't it taught: [If] one was sleeping in a bed and the members of his household, etc." - Rashi explained: His wife is included in "his household." But this does not appear correct: First, for we do not find that his wife is called "members of his household" [benei veito]; and furthermore, according to his explanation, [the Gemara] should have said, "And behold, it is taught here," since it refers to the baraita [cited] above; but from the fact that it says, "And wasn't it taught," this implies that it is a different baraita. And Harav Yosef says that we read: "[If] one was sleeping in a bed and his wife was sleeping beside him, he may not turn his face and recite [Shema] unless a garment was separating between him and her."
